title: graphify skill + /graph command to use the knowledge graph in a project
description: The framework has its own knowledge graph (src/knowledge-graph.js with loadGraph/addNode/addEdge/removeNode/removeEdge/neighbors/nodesByType, plus /graph and /api/graph views on the board server), but no user-facing skill or slash command to drive it from a project. Ship (1) a graphify Agent Skill under skills/graphify/SKILL.md (byte-identical parity copy in .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md) with progressive-disclosure frontmatter describing WHEN to load it, teaching the orchestrator to build/query/inspect the graph via the existing knowledge-graph.js API; and (2) a commands/graph.md slash command (/agentic-framework:graph) that launches the board server and opens the /graph view (like /agentic-framework:console / task-status). RESPECT the recorded design decision (2026-06-11): the graph is an INCREMENTAL INDEX over existing artifacts (knowledge_entry, task, decision, skill nodes + typed edges), NOT a bulk re-scanner and NOT a second copy of state — the skill drives the incremental add/query API and visualization, it does not introduce a bulk artifact-scanner. No new src/ engine logic. This is the framework's OWN graphify, distinct from the unrelated gsd-graphify skill.
acceptance_criteria: skills/graphify/SKILL.md exists with frontmatter whose description clearly states WHEN to load the skill (progressive disclosure), and a byte-identical parity copy exists at .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md (locked by the skills-parity test pattern).

The skill documents the knowledge-graph.js public API (loadGraph/addNode/addEdge/removeNode/removeEdge/neighbors/nodesByType), the node types and typed edges, and gives concrete how-to recipes for build/query/inspect against a project's knowledge/graph/graph.json.
The skill explicitly states the incremental-index design boundary: it does not bulk-rescan artifacts or duplicate state; it indexes existing artifacts via incremental edges.

commands/graph.md exists, is auto-discovered as /agentic-framework:graph, and launches node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/task-board.cjs then directs the user to the /graph view (consistent with the console/task-status command pattern).
Any skill-parity / command-manifest tests pass; npm run test:changed plus affected e2e specs are green.
UAT: loading the skill, the orchestrator can add a node + edge and query neighbors on a scratch graph, and /agentic-framework:graph opens the graph view in the browser.
